description: Sync channel posts and replies from the teams you choose, and the chats of the people you choose, one document per message. Team, channel and chat membership restricts search when Enforce ACL is on and HydraDB can read the members.
opening: Sync channel posts and replies from the Microsoft Teams teams you select, and the 1:1, group and meeting chats of the people you select. Each post, reply and chat message is one document. A reply links to its root post and a chat message to its chat, so a conversation is returned together. Text from PDF and DOCX files shared in messages is searchable when HydraDB can download and read the files.

With Enforce ACL on, a standard channel's messages can be read by the team's members, a private or shared channel's messages by that channel's members, and a chat's messages by its participants. Private and shared channels are skipped unless you turn on `include_private_channels`. Chats need the optional `Chat.Read.All` permission. Every sync fails until Microsoft approves your app for the Teams protected APIs. A message deleted in Teams becomes a hidden stub rather than being removed.

permissions.who_can_read: A standard channel's messages can be read by the team's members. A private or shared channel's messages can be read by that channel's members, including the members of every team a shared channel is shared with. A chat's messages can be read by its participants.
permissions.identity: A member's email address, in lower case.
permissions.when_unreadable: If a team, channel or chat member list is missing, empty or cannot be read in full, the message is marked with a permission warning, which you can find with `additional_metadata.rbac_warning`. A partial member list is never applied.
notes: A team or channel with more than 5,000 members cannot be captured. Set an access rule on such a team.
Do not rely on a team or channel membership change to update access right away.

connect.auth: Microsoft Teams uses a Microsoft Entra ID app registration with application permissions and a client secret. The same app can also back an Outlook connector.

credentials.name: client_secret
credentials.text: The client secret's Value, shown once in the Azure portal.

settings.name: include_private_channels
settings.text: Set to `true` to also sync private and shared channels, restricted to their members. Off by default.

connect.permissions_label: Microsoft Graph application permissions to grant

permissions.name: Team.ReadBasic.All
permissions.text: lists the tenant's teams and reads each selected team's name.

permissions.name: Channel.ReadBasic.All
permissions.text: lists the channels of each selected team.

permissions.name: ChannelMessage.Read.All
permissions.text: reads channel posts and replies. A Teams protected API.

permissions.name: TeamMember.Read.All
permissions.text: reads each team's members, who can read its standard channels.

permissions.name: ChannelMember.Read.All
permissions.text: reads private and shared channel members, and the teams a channel is shared with.

permissions.name: User.ReadBasic.All
permissions.text: lists people for chat selection, and resolves authors to names and addresses.

permissions.name: Chat.Read.All
permissions.text: optional. Reads the chats of the people you select. A Teams protected API. Without it, no chats are offered.

permissions.name: Files.Read.All
permissions.text: optional. Lets HydraDB download PDF and DOCX files shared in messages. Messages sync without it, but without the file text.

connect.permissions_note: Request access to the Teams protected APIs at https://aka.ms/teamsgraph/requestaccess with your app id and tenant id. Until Microsoft approves the app, every Teams sync fails with a 403 error, even though the permissions show as granted.

steps.title: Register an app
steps.text: In Microsoft Entra ID, register an app with no redirect URI and create a client secret. Copy the tenant id, the client id and the secret's Value.

steps.title: Grant permissions
steps.text: Add the Microsoft Graph application permissions above, not delegated ones, and grant admin consent.

steps.title: Request protected API access
steps.text: Request access to the Teams protected APIs with your app id and tenant id, and wait for Microsoft's approval.

steps.title: Create the connector
steps.text: Enter `tenant`, `client_id` and `client_secret`. Set `include_private_channels` to `true` to also sync private and shared channels.

steps.title: Select teams and people
steps.text: HydraDB lists the tenant's teams and users. Select the teams whose channels to sync. Select a person to sync the chats that person takes part in. Chats are opted in person by person.

steps.title: Rotate the secret
steps.text: Rotate the client secret before it expires. An expired secret stops every sync.

connect.account: One connector reads the teams and people you select in one Microsoft 365 tenant.

sync.first_sync: Each selected team and person reaches back the window set by `lookback_days`, 30 days by default.
sync.changes: Each sync reads the messages modified since the last sync, per team and per selected person's chats. A channel post with a new reply is picked up again, even if the post itself is old.
sync.edits: An edited message is read again and replaces its document. A new reply also makes its root post be read again.
sync.deletes: A message deleted in Teams is replaced on the next sync by a stub with the text `[deleted]`. With Enforce ACL on, nobody can read the stub. The document itself is not removed.

shared_attributes.name: author
shared_attributes.text: The display name of the person or bot that posted, written as the From line. The graph records the message as sent by that author.

shared_attributes.name: created_at
shared_attributes.text: When the message was posted, written as the Sent line.

shared_attributes.name: updated_at
shared_attributes.text: When the message was last modified. Not searchable.

shared_attributes.name: mentions
shared_attributes.text: The names of the people, bots or channels @mentioned. The graph records each as mentioned. This list is not searchable by itself, but the names stay in the message text.

shared_attributes.name: attachments
shared_attributes.text: The names of attached files, cards or links. They are searchable only when the message has no text, as its `Shared:` line. Text read from supported files is searchable separately.

shared_attributes.name: additional_metadata.has_attachments
shared_attributes.text: `true` when the message has a non-inline attachment. Not searchable.

shared_attributes.name: additional_metadata.from_application
shared_attributes.text: `true` when a bot posted the message. Excludes or isolates bot posts. Not searchable.

shared_attributes.name: additional_metadata.rbac_warning
shared_attributes.text: Present when the message's member list could not be read in full. Finds such messages. Not searchable.

shared_attributes.name: additional_metadata.is_deleted
shared_attributes.text: `true` on the hidden stub left by a deleted message. Not searchable.

shared_attributes.name: connector_id
shared_attributes.text: Limits a query to this connector's messages. Not searchable.

shared_attributes.name: edited_at
shared_attributes.text: When the message was last edited.

shared_attributes.name: reaction_count
shared_attributes.text: How many reactions the message has.

shared_attributes.name: importance
shared_attributes.text: `high`, `low` or `urgent`, when the message's importance is not normal.

documents.name: Channel messages
documents.one_document: One root post in a channel, or one reply.
documents.title: The post's subject, else the first line of its text cut to about 120 characters, else `Teams message` and its id. Search matches the message text, not this title, so a subject is searchable only when it also appears in the text.
documents.text: The message flattened from HTML, with @mention tags shown as the mentioned name. A post with no text but with attachments reads `Shared:` followed by the attachment names. The author is written as a From line and the posted time as a Sent line.
documents.date: When the message was last modified, else when it was posted.
documents.files: Attachment names are kept. Text from PDF and DOCX files up to 50 MiB is searchable separately when `Files.Read.All` is granted and HydraDB can download and read the files. Images embedded in a message are not read.

attributes.name: parent_id
attributes.text: For a reply, the root post it answers. Joins the reply to that post, so the whole conversation can be returned together. Not searchable.

attributes.name: thread_id
attributes.text: The root post's id. Groups a root post and its replies into one thread. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.container_id
attributes.text: The channel's id. Limits a query to one channel. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.container_name
attributes.text: The channel's name. Limits a query to one channel by name. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.container_type
attributes.text: Always `channel`. Separates channel messages from chat messages. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.team_id
attributes.text: The team's id. Limits a query to one team. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.team_name
attributes.text: The team's name. Limits a query to one team by name. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.channel_membership_type
attributes.text: `standard`, `private` or `shared`. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.is_reply
attributes.text: `true` for replies. Keeps only root posts or only replies. Not searchable.

attributes.name: Team or channel
attributes.text: For a standard channel, the team's members can read the message. For a private or shared channel, the channel's members can. Not searchable.

attributes.name: reply_count
attributes.text: How many replies a root post had when it was synced.

documents.name: Chat messages
documents.one_document: One message in a 1:1, group or meeting chat.
documents.title: The first line of the text cut to about 120 characters, else `Teams chat message` and its id. Search matches the message text, not this title.
documents.text: The message flattened from HTML, or `Shared:` followed by the attachment names when there is no text. The author is written as a From line and the sent time as a Sent line.
documents.date: When the message was last modified, else when it was sent.
documents.files: Attachment names are kept. Text from PDF and DOCX files up to 50 MiB is searchable separately when `Files.Read.All` is granted and HydraDB can download and read the files. Images embedded in a message are not read.

attributes.name: thread_id
attributes.text: The chat's id. Groups all messages of one chat into one thread. Not searchable.

attributes.name: parent_id
attributes.text: Also the chat's id. Keeps a chat's messages together, so earlier messages are read as context. The chat itself is not a document. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.container_id
attributes.text: The chat's id. Limits a query to one chat. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.container_name
attributes.text: The chat's topic, or up to four participant names. Limits a query to one chat by name. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.container_type
attributes.text: Always `chat`. Separates chat messages from channel messages. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.chat_type
attributes.text: `oneOnOne`, `group` or `meeting`. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.is_reply
attributes.text: Always `false` for chat messages. Not searchable.

attributes.name: Chat
attributes.text: The chat's participants can read its messages. Not searchable.

attributes.name: participants
attributes.text: The names of the chat's participants. They are not attached to the message in the graph.

example_searches: What did the Platform team decide in the incidents channel about the database migration?
What did Alex say in our 1:1 chat about the launch date?
Show the replies to the post announcing the new on-call rotation.

connections: A channel reply to its root post.
Every chat message to its chat, so a chat's messages are kept together.
A message to any Loom video it links to, which resolves when that video is synced into the same collection.
No other links to other tools.
people: The people, bots and channels @mentioned in a message.
Chat participants are kept with each chat message but not attached in the graph.

not_synced: Private and shared channels, unless `include_private_channels` is on.
Chats of people you did not select, and every chat without `Chat.Read.All`.
Shared file formats other than PDF and DOCX, and images embedded in a message.
